file uses measured x1.5, to two significant figures), never a round

mechanism with no instance is documentation rotting in place -- which is

which variable, which leaf property call, and what the third-party
oracle says -- so a future session can tell a golden-side artifact from

Rules for adding an absolute entry, on top of the four above:
* `unit` is mandatory. The harness cannot check it -- an absolute
tolerance is dimensional and the number is unreadable without it.
* `measured` is per variable, and `absolute` must cover it. Same x1.5

* ABS_TOL (1e-12) < `absolute` < ABS_CEILING (1e-4). Below the floor the
harness already accepts the difference and the entry changes nothing.
The ceiling is argued in kelvin because that is the unit every instance

more than the ceiling is claiming a bigger oracle artifact than any yet
measured and owes fresh evidence, not a bigger number. The eight

* `absolute` <= 2 x |golden| for that variable, checked at replay. This
is what makes the channel self-limiting: where the true value is zero
the golden IS the oracle's error, so forgiving more than twice it stops
forgiving the oracle's artifact and starts hiding this engine's. It
also means the channel can never be pointed at a healthy variable in
order to widen it. The x1.5 rule leaves ~33% of slack under this bound,
deliberately. One limit follows and is accepted: a golden of exactly
0.0 admits no entry at all -- if the PORT returns more than 1e-12 where
the oracle returns a true zero, the artifact is on this side.

dead relative entry does; so does a variable the golden does not have,
